blocks.x: IoT, Twin & Robotics applied to Semiconductors & Hardware. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

Hardware companies run the longest R&D loops under the sharpest IP threats: design simulation, fab yield (their own or partners'), supply-chain visibility and product security. Compute acceleration and governed data are the compounding assets.

items: Multi-tier supply opaque; allocation shocks disrupt.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Industrial IoT & sensor network, Industrial IoT & sensor network, Computer Vision & Edge AI from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Design/simulation, Supply-chain visibility, Yield analytics) on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — Export controls among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Your product becomes a service: device fleets, OTA and telemetry products with revenue attached.
Facilities that run themselves: BMS/IoT fusion, energy optimization and city-scale platforms.
Sense everything that matters: retrofit-friendly sensor network with governed telemetry.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Technology & SaaS level this capability reads as: energy and utilization telemetry for sites (operating cost down measurably). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
